comparator.route: Economics and Business Economics discipline route
comparator.sourceNotes: Reconstructed from the 2026-2027 Teaching and Examination Regulations for RIO programme 57084, published on the current ESPhil programme-regulations page. The TER defines a 180-EC curriculum consisting of 90 EC in one chosen academic discipline, 60 EC of eight named common philosophy courses, 15 EC of discipline-specific philosophy electives, and a 15-EC bachelor-thesis and milestones trajectory linking both fields. The normalized target is generic and does not name a discipline. The Economics and Business Economics route is instantiated under the neutral route rule: the TER lists Erasmus School of Economics first among the eligible EUR schools, and its broad Economics and Business Economics bachelor is selected rather than a narrower specialist programme. This choice was fixed independently of UCR fit. The 90-EC discipline component and the 15-EC discipline-specific philosophy component are preserved at their official structural weights. The public curriculum describes the economics programme's foundations, while the exact 2026 discipline-elective pair is available only through MyEUR; no unpublished course choice or EC subdivision is invented.

comparatorRouteSelection.route: Economics and Business Economics discipline route
comparatorRouteSelection.basis: The generic target permits several chosen disciplines. No discipline represents the programme more strongly than the others. The TER lists Erasmus School of Economics first among the eligible EUR schools, and Economics and Business Economics is the broad, general economics-and-business bachelor rather than a specialist ESE programme. It is therefore selected by the neutral least-specialized and official-order rules, before and independently of UCR course selection.

progressionAssessment.rationale: Introduction to Western Philosophy, Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations and Introduction to Economics establish the two programme strands in semester 1. Research Methods & Statistics precedes every economics course that formally requires it, while Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations precedes Transnational Business Law, International Business & Governance and Money, Banking & Finance. The 100-level rhetoric course precedes Persuasive Communication. Ethics and Philosophy of Mind precede the 300-level philosophy courses conceptually. The final semester brings together econometrics, behavioural economics, finance and qualitative methodology. Every course is available in its assigned term and every formal prerequisite is completed in an earlier semester.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The closest match owns the generic programme interests, the common philosophy core, the Liberal Arts and Sciences combination, and the two economics/business directions represented by the neutrally selected comparator route. Two further coherent generator-backed directions remain. Social and behavioural sciences, law, international social challenges, global power and sociology form one institutional route, included as Philosophy, Society & Law. Medicine and healthcare form a second route, included as Philosophy, Health & Human Existence. Both are mechanically feasible and qualitatively distinct; the pairwise differences are 13 courses between the first two alternatives and 16 courses for each pair involving the health alternative. The history, culture and communication direction is separately recorded but is not pursued after the maximum of three included alternatives is reached.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both introduce major Western philosophical traditions and the historical development of philosophical questions; the Erasmus component concentrates on the Enlightenment while UCR provides the broader introduction.
Both examine what it means to be human through mind, consciousness and personal identity.
Both are the central moral-philosophy component, joining ethical theory to contemporary applied questions.
Both examine technology philosophically. UCR concentrates on artificial intelligence, human flourishing, fairness and responsibility rather than art and media more broadly.

Theoretical Analytic Philosophy is a dedicated survey of analytic philosophy. UCR distributes related work across philosophy of mind, metaphysics and political philosophy and has no single equivalent course.
The comparator includes a dedicated Philosophy of Science course. UCR teaches research methods and evidence evaluation but no philosophy-of-science course, so the component is left unmatched.
The comparator provides a systematic historical epistemology course. UCR's introductory philosophy course is already aligned with Enlightenment, and no separate UCR epistemology course exists.

The comparator requires a 15-EC independent thesis integrating philosophy and the chosen discipline. None of the 24 scheduled UCR courses is a thesis, so it is recorded as unmatched; UCR's optional independent-research element is displayed alongside it.

The comparator's chosen-discipline component comprises 90 EC of Economics and Business Economics coursework. It is preserved as the official 90-EC component rather than equated with one UCR course; the UCR economics and business courses appear separately in this block.

The comparator reserves 15 EC for philosophy courses tailored to economics. UCR combines philosophy and economics across separate courses but has no verified equivalent 15-EC discipline-philosophy package.
Both are political-philosophy components examining authority, society and critique through major arguments and thinkers.

notes.text: The Rotterdam programme combines 90 EC from a separate chosen discipline with a structured 60-EC philosophy core, 15 EC of philosophy tailored to that discipline, and a 15-EC integrative thesis. UCR instead combines individual philosophy courses directly with courses from economics and business, law and society, or health and biomedicine. UCR offers philosophy in ethics, mind, emotion, agency, political thought, human rights and AI, but it does not reproduce Rotterdam's dedicated sequence in analytic philosophy, epistemology and philosophy of science or its discipline-specific philosophy package.
